title: AuditRecord
description: One record of an audit chain (ADR 0069). A chain is one JSON Lines stream owned by one writer; each line is one record, and a record's hash is the SHA-256 of its line's exact UTF-8 bytes without the line feed. Every record carries its chain's id, its sequence from zero, a timestamp and the hash of the record before it. A chain's first record opens it, naming its writer and the chain it continues; after that a record is evidence of a governance mutation, evidence of a read, or a signed head over the records before it.

OpenRecord.description: A chain's first record, and only its first: it names the writer the chain belongs to and, where that writer had an earlier chain, the chain this one continues. It is what lets a chain be opened, linked to its predecessor and signed before any governance action happens, which is how a writer that restarts freezes the tail its last process left unsigned.

MutationRecord.description: The governance audit's record (ADR 0038): who did what to which governed resource, in which tenant and environment, with what outcome, a refused action included. Nothing else is recorded, so the record is payload-safe by construction.

ReadRecord.description: The read-side audit's record (ADR 0070): who read, or tried to read, which resource, and at which disclosure tier. It carries the same subject and dimensions as a mutation record and lands in the same chain. It names the actor, the target and the tier, never what was read, so it is payload-safe for the same reason a mutation record is.

HeadRecord.description: A signed head: the writer's signature over its chain so far. The signature covers a statement of the chain's id, this record's sequence and this record's previous-hash, which is the hash of the last record before the head, so it vouches for every record before it. Heads are what show an alteration or a removal at a chain's tail, which the hash links alone cannot.

HeadSignature.description: A head's signature, in the executor package signing stack's form (ADR 0025), under the audit's own key.

ChainId.description: The chain's id: 32 lowercase hex digits, a version 7 UUID minted by the writer when it opens the chain, so a writer's chains sort by when they were opened. Every record of a chain carries the same id.

Sequence.description: The record's position in its chain, from zero, with no gaps.

Timestamp.description: When the writer appended the record.

RecordHash.description: A record hash: the SHA-256 of a record line's UTF-8 bytes, as 64 lowercase hex digits. A chain's first record carries 64 zeros.

Label.description: A controlled-vocabulary name or an identifier. Never a workflow payload or a secret.

ChainContinuation.description: Carried by the open record of a chain whose writer had an earlier chain: the earlier chain's id and the hash of the last record of it the writer knows of. In a running process that is the last record the writer stored, held in memory; after a restart it is the last whole record the writer read back from the sink. A writer opens a new chain when an append fails, since the failed chain's tail is then unknown, when a chain reaches its record limit, and when it starts.

WriterId.description: The id of the writer a chain belongs to: one control plane instance, stable across its restarts. A writer's chains are stored under its id, and a writer only ever continues its own.
